children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Monday.
WHEAT - Up 4 to 7 cents per bushel
rose after drone attacks by Ukraine and Russia reduced hopes for a de-escalation in their war which has virtually stopped their Black Sea exports.
However, Russia is working closely with Turkey to ensure the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, the Interfax news agency cited Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova as saying on Monday.

Russian wheat export prices fell last week in line with global markets, and analysts are revising their estimates for shipments from Russia in September upwards, although they remain at multi-year lows.

Egypt is diversifying its source of wheat imports towards France and other European suppliers, moving away from Ukraine and Russia where supplies have been disrupted, Supply Minister Sherif Farouk was quoted as saying on Sunday.
Wheat was underpinned by importer demand, with Pakistan buying 365,000 tons on Saturday  and then issuing a tender to buy 185,000 tons on Sunday.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was 7-1/2 cents higher to $7.21-3/4 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was up 7-1/4 cents to $7.91 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last 7-1/4 cents higher to $7.48-1/2 a bushel.
CORN - Up 3 to 5 cents per bushel
turned higher on spillover support from soybean and wheat futures.
Planting of Brazil's 2026/27 first corn crop reached 27% of the estimated area in the center-south region, compared with 22% a week earlier and 25% a year ago.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last 5-3/4 cents higher to $5.33-1/4 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Up 7 to 10 cents per bushel
rose on Monday as traders await a meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, which could generate more Chinese buying of US supplies.

Brazilian farmers had planted 1.2% of the expected area for their 2026/27 soybean crop as of last Thursday, agribusiness consultancy AgRural said on Monday, up from 0.4% a week earlier and ahead of the 0.9% registered a year ago.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last 10-1/2 cents higher to $13.14 per bushel.
